content.value_statement: iOS simulator testing often needs repeatable taps, gestures, captures, and accessibility inspection. This skill provides AXe CLI command patterns that help Claude, Codex, and Claude Code drive simulator workflows.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install AXe and list iOS Simulator UDIDs.
Documents tap, swipe, touch, gesture, and hardware button commands.
Provides text input, keycode, key sequence, and file-based typing examples.
Explains screenshot capture, MP4 recording, MJPEG streaming, and ffmpeg piping.
Shows accessibility tree inspection for full screens and specific points.
Includes automation patterns for wait-then-tap, scroll-to-find, form filling, and post-action screenshots.
limitations: Requires macOS, Apple iOS Simulator, Homebrew, and the AXe CLI.
Does not install or manage simulators, apps, or test accounts by itself.
Examples use placeholder UDIDs, labels, coordinates, and file names that must be adapted.
Screenshots, recordings, and accessibility trees may contain sensitive app data.

use_cases.title: Run repeatable simulator flows
use_cases.description: Drive taps, swipes, gestures, and buttons during manual or assisted iOS app testing.

use_cases.title: Inspect accessibility surfaces
use_cases.description: Review labels, identifiers, and point-based UI details before fixing accessibility issues.

use_cases.title: Capture reproduction evidence
use_cases.description: Create screenshots, videos, and streamed recordings after specific simulator actions.

prompt_templates.title: Start simulator automation
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simulator session
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the AXe steps to list simulators, choose a UDID, and run one safe tap command.

prompt_templates.title: Tap and type through a form
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an AXe command sequence that taps fields by label, enters test text, and submits the form on my selected simulator.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a difficult UI element
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me use AXe to inspect the accessibility tree and identify the best selector for a button that is hard to tap.

prompt_templates.title: Build a capture workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an AXe workflow that performs a gesture sequence, waits for the result, captures a screenshot, and records a short video.

output_examples.input: I need to tap a visible Continue button and capture the next screen.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the simulator UDID requirement, recommends tapping by label, adds a short post-action delay, and saves a screenshot with a clear file name.

output_examples.input: I cannot find the right accessibility identifier for a control.
output_examples.output: The response suggests describing the full UI tree, narrowing by screen position, and using a stable label or identifier before falling back to coordinates.

output_examples.input: I need evidence of a scrolling bug.
output_examples.output: The response outlines a repeatable gesture sequence, a short recording setup, and a final screenshot for comparison.

best_practices: Confirm the simulator UDID and app state before running automation commands.
Prefer accessibility identifiers or labels over coordinates when they are stable.
Review screenshots, recordings, and UI descriptions for sensitive data before sharing them.
anti_patterns: Running commands against a guessed or stale simulator UDID.
Hardcoding production credentials in form-filling examples.
Assuming coordinate-based taps will work across every simulator size and orientation.

faq.question: What does this skill help automate?
faq.answer: It helps generate AXe CLI command patterns for iOS Simulator taps, gestures, typing, screenshots, video, and accessibility inspection.

faq.question: Does it work on physical iPhones?
faq.answer: No. The documented AXe commands target Apple iOS Simulator workflows, not physical device automation.

faq.question: Do I need AXe installed first?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes a Homebrew installation command, but AXe must be available before commands can run.

faq.question: Can it choose the right simulator automatically?
faq.answer: It shows how to list simulators and set a UDID. You still need to select the correct running simulator.

faq.question: Can it inspect accessibility information?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents commands for full-screen accessibility trees and point-based UI descriptions.

faq.question: What should I protect when using captures?
faq.answer: Treat screenshots, videos, streams, and UI trees as sensitive when the simulator shows private app data.
